items.title: Google Announces Major Core Update for March 2026
items.summary: Google launched its March 2026 core update, emphasizing quality signals and superior user experience to refine search relevance, with rollout expected to take up to three weeks. The update reinforces E-E-A-T principles, potentially causing ranking fluctuations for low-quality content while rewarding genuine expertise. SEOs are advised to audit pages for E-E-A-T, monitor Search Console, and prioritize helpful content and UX metrics.

items.title: Google Tests Ask Maps: AI-Powered Conversational Search in Maps
items.summary: Google is testing 'Ask Maps,' a Gemini AI feature in Google Maps for complex place-based queries like nearby dining options, providing direct AI-generated answers. This enhances local discovery but may alter traffic by reducing multi-step searches. Businesses should optimize profiles for better visibility in these AI recommendations.

items.title: Google Rolls Out Branded Queries Filter and AI Mode Insights in Search Console
items.summary: Google expanded the AI-powered branded queries filter in Search Console to all eligible sites, automating classification including typos for better traffic analysis. Meanwhile, AI Mode self-citations have risen to 21%, directing more links to Google properties and potentially reducing external traffic. Ask Maps also launched, boosting conversational local search.

items.title: Google’s John Mueller: Optimize for AI Search Visibility Beyond Traditional SEO
items.summary: John Mueller advises businesses reliant on referred traffic to consider AI's role in visibility across Google Search, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, and others, regardless of terminology like GEO. AI favors well-ranking pages with clear entities, comparisons, and brand attribution. Strategies include structured content for extraction, entity building, and authoritative backlinks.

items.title: Top SEO & AI Search News: Branded Queries, AI Linking, Technical SEO for AI - March 15
items.summary: Aleyda Solis' weekly roundup covers Google expanding branded queries in Search Console, Robby Stein on AI linking, crawlers video, Perplexity court case, keyword semantics in 2026, and technical optimizations for AI crawlers. Highlights include Digital PR for AI citations and SaaS docs for visibility. Emphasizes machine-readable content to avoid invisibility.

items.title: March 2026 Core Update Cracks Down on Boring, Mass-Produced AI Content
items.summary: The March 2026 Core Update penalizes generic AI-generated content, ending the copy-paste era and rewarding unique insights from experience. Agencies use AI with quality checks, but small businesses win by adding personal data and missing perspectives from top rankings. Focus on voice-infused, non-boring content for EEAT.

items.title: Journalist Accuses Grammarly of AI Impersonation in Editing Feature
items.summary: Tech journalist Ray Wong calls out Grammarly for using his name and Gizmodo affiliation in its AI 'Expert Review' feature, which scrapes writers' work to mimic editing suggestions. He labels it identity theft and criticizes the company's disclaimer as insufficient amid widespread backlash. The viral post with over 680 likes sparks calls for lawsuits and ethical reforms in AI writing tools.

items.title: Publishers Weekly Reports Major Book Deals for Week of March 16
items.summary: Publishers Weekly highlights recent acquisitions: W.W. Norton buys Tonya Mosley’s memoir 'In Case of My Death' at auction for U.S., Canada, and open market rights. Grove Atlantic secures world English rights to Mariia Niskavaara’s debut novel 'Esther, the Butcher', sold in 17 territories. Hanover Square acquires a two-book horror deal for Kylie Lee Baker’s 'Hell to Pay'.

items.title: Scarlett Press Secures Six-Figure Pre-Empt Deal for Georgia Bowers' Supernatural Romances
items.summary: The Bookseller announces Scarlett Press, Simon & Schuster UK imprint, acquiring two books from author Georgia Bowers in a six-figure pre-empt at London Book Fair. The lead title 'Only Fangs' features a conflicted vampire in a supernatural romance, slated for paperback in July 2027. This deal signals strong publisher interest in genre fiction.

items.title: Grammarly Removes AI Expert Review Feature Mimicking Writers After Backlash
items.summary: Grammarly removed its AI Expert Review feature that generated editing suggestions inspired by styles of figures like Stephen King and Neil deGrasse Tyson due to backlash over unauthorized identity use. Journalist Julia Angwin filed a class-action lawsuit against parent Superhuman for unlawfully monetizing names without consent, seeking over $5 million. CEO apologized, promising redesign while defending legally.

items.title: AI Fuels Surge in Self-Publishing Scams Targeting Authors
items.summary: Fraudsters leverage AI for personalized scams promising self-publishers bestseller status and marketing for upfront fees, as retired teacher Jon Cocks lost nearly A$10,000 to fake services. Originating from south Asia, Philippines, and Nigeria, these operations deliver worthless AI-generated content and extort victims, with over 2,500 scam publishers identified last year. The boom exploits authors' inexperience in the growing self-publishing market.

items.title: Official BookTok Chart to Launch in the UK
items.summary: The UK will introduce an official BookTok Top 20 chart later this year, blending retail sales data with TikTok engagement via NielsenIQ BookData and Media Control algorithms weighted toward sales. Following a successful German pilot, it formalizes BookTok's influence on book trends and sales. Publishers recognize social media as a key driver in the international market.

items.title: Jean Smart Blasted for Getting Teary-Eyed While 'Spewing Woke' Comments at Golden Globes
items.summary: Jean Smart drew criticism for her emotional political remarks during an interview on the 2026 Golden Globes red carpet with Variety. Viewers accused her of preaching woke ideology amid tears. The comments sparked backlash online against Hollywood's political posturing.

items.title: Oscars 2026: Has Hollywood's 'Wokeism' Run Its Course?
items.summary: The 2026 Oscars faced scrutiny over persistent woke elements in Hollywood productions and ceremonies. Social media users labeled the industry as full of 'narcissists acting like activists,' with trends like 'Oscars woke' gaining traction. Audience fatigue with political messaging appears to be growing.

items.title: Live Nation Employees Bragged About Gouging Customers in Court Documents
items.summary: Unsealed court documents revealed Live Nation staff joking about high fees and ability to 'gouge' ticket buyers. The revelations from the entertainment giant behind Ticketmaster fueled public outrage over pricing practices. Customers expressed anger at exploitative tactics in the industry.

items.title: Wokeness Dwindles as Brands and Hollywood Retreat from DEI Initiatives
items.summary: A viral post highlights corporations like Target, Bud Light, and Netflix abandoning DEI, race-based hiring, and related mandates following public pushback. The shift marks the culture war's end with the silent majority turning vocal against woke policies. Hollywood's potential under woke leadership is cited as averted disaster.

items.title: Fans Slam Awards Shows for Woke Sermons and Virtue Signaling
items.summary: A user laments the loss of glamour in awards shows due to condescending woke lectures and moralizing from Hollywood elites. The constant virtue signaling alienates average viewers who reject the hypocrisy. Many report tuning out entirely in rebellion.

items.title: ENHYPEN Fans Furious at BELIFT for Profiting Off Heeseung While Erasing Him from Content
items.summary: ENGENEs rage against BELIFT LAB for including Heeseung in sales promotions after removing him from group activities, calling it exploitation of OT7. Fans protest outside HYBE demanding his return, affirming 'ENHYPEN IS SEVEN.' Jake's confirmation of performance changes intensified accusations of erasure.

items.title: AI Presents a Major Opportunity for Small Businesses—But Support Needed
items.summary: A Goldman Sachs insight reveals that 93% of small businesses using AI report a positive impact on their operations. Despite this, 85% support the proposed AI for Main Street Act to provide necessary training and resources. This highlights AI's transformative potential for SMBs if barriers like skills gaps are addressed.

items.title: Mega AI is Leveling the Playing Field for SMBs with its AI Growth Engine
items.summary: SignalFire spotlights Mega AI, an innovative tool designed to help small-to-medium businesses tackle marketing challenges. By providing clear ROI insights and automation, it empowers SMB owners previously hindered by opaque ad spending. This represents a significant product move making enterprise-level growth accessible to smaller players.

items.title: 28 AI Tools That Could Save You Thousands of Hours for Your Business
items.summary: Entrepreneur Adam Muhammad Mukhtar lists 28 practical AI tools for business automation, from Claude and ChatGPT for content to HeyGen for videos and Clay for sales outreach. These tools cover every business aspect, enabling solopreneurs and SMBs to boost productivity massively. High engagement shows real interest in actionable AI stacks.

items.title: 10 Ways Small Businesses Are Using AI Right Now That Large Corporations Haven’t Figured Out
items.summary: Incognito Learners details how SMBs lead AI adoption with applications like AI phone agents, cash flow forecasting, automated hiring, and competitor monitoring. Unlike big corps bogged down by bureaucracy, small businesses act fast, seeing revenue boosts and hiring growth. This thread emphasizes AI's role in giving SMBs a competitive edge.
